business_profile.text:
GE Aerospace (General Electric Company) is a world-class aerospace propulsion leader designing, manufacturing, and servicing commercial and military aircraft jet engines, avionics, and power systems. Operating as a standalone aviation pure-play, the company powers three out of every four commercial airline flights worldwide through its proprietary engines (GE90, GE9X, GEnx) and its 50/50 CFM International joint venture with Safran (CFM56 and LEAP engine families).

GE Aerospace operates a highly lucrative razor-and-blade business model: engines are sold at competitive initial pricing, locking in multi-decade, high-margin aftermarket spare parts, maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services under long-term time-and-materials or power-by-the-hour contracts. Management is ramping production of the fuel-efficient LEAP engine for the Airbus A320neo and Boeing 737 MAX families while advancing next-generation hybrid-electric and open-fan RISE engine technologies.

competitive_moat_analysis.text: GE Aerospace commands an exceptional economic moat built on an installed base of more than 44,000 commercial engines and 26,000 military aircraft engines, immense FAA certification barriers, and multi-decade aftermarket service agreements. Developing and certifying a commercial jet engine requires billions in R&D and over a decade of regulatory testing, creating near-total duopoly market dynamics. Airlines face prohibitive aircraft modification costs to switch engine suppliers, guaranteeing GE Aerospace highly recurring, high-margin aftermarket cash flow spanning 30-year engine lifecycles.
